strategy.action_description: Use f1aa1c2d as the grouped-GEMM parent, but change only FP4 load/dequant inside its stage1_grouped_gemm_kernel and stage2_grouped_gemm_kernel. Replace the switch-based scalar load_fp4_scaled path with d660c1aa-style scale-tiled helpers: one scale load per scale vector, constant/LUT or branchless e2m1 decode, aligned packed uint32/uint4 loads with byte fallbacks, and K-split-safe handling when a cooperative lane begins inside a scale tile. Preserve the existing route grouping, 8x16 tiles, 4-way K split, atomics, and output semantics.
strategy.evidence_chain: The grouped GEMM parent already improved the scalar baseline to 247.424 us, but its kernel still calls a scalar switch decoder for every FP4 nibble. The d660c1aa dequant-only parent cut latency to 223.744 us by replacing scalar per-element decode with scale-tiled packed loads. New finding: the local wiki vectorized-load guidance calls out FP4's 0.5-byte element size as requiring wide loads, and the compute-capability table says CC 8.9 has BF16/FP8 tensor cores but no FP4 tensor cores, so this CUDA target still needs efficient software FP4 decode inside any grouped GEMM.
strategy.expected_impact: Medium to high. This is the cleanest combination of the two successful generation-1 ideas: keep f1aa1c2d's additional GEMM parallelism while removing its remaining scalar decode overhead. It should be especially useful if qwen_micro or TP2-like shapes expose more K work per tile.
strategy.risks: K-split lanes cross scale-vector boundaries, so blindly copying d660c1aa helpers can apply the wrong scale. Wider decode tiles may raise register pressure in the already larger grouped-GEMM kernels. Roll back to f1aa1c2d scalar load_fp4_scaled if occupancy or correctness regresses.
